limits: The search allowance for the turn (200 searches) ran out: second-pass checks were cut short in every slice, and entertainment (theaters, attractions, streaming, tickets) was not searched at all (one finding).

C: Black Friday week sale events of clot.notes: METHOD AND LIMITS. (1) Only 21 web searches ran. Four further batched searches (covering Under Armour, Columbia, The North Face, Patagonia, Carhartt, L.L.Bean, New Balance, HOKA, Gap, Gap Factory, J.Crew, Abercrombie, Hollister, H&M, Levi's, Walgreens, CVS, Sephora, Victoria's Secret, GNC, Vitamin Shoppe, iHerb, Peloton, Garmin, Fitbit, Oral-B, Sonicare, Foot Locker, Finish Line, Famous Footwear, Zappos, UGG, Fanatics) were refused because the web-search allowance shared by all the searchers in this run was used up. Coverage of the slice is therefore partial, and an empty result for a store means 'not found in what ran', not 'no event'. (2) No web page could be opened: oldnavy.gap.com, www.ulta.com, www.rei.com and visualping.io all failed to resolve because they are outside this session's allowed network domains, so I stopped trying. Everything here comes from search results. (3) Because of (2), every 'quote' is the wording shown in the search result for that page; where the search tool summarised a page rather than showing its text, the quote is that summary's wording, and it may not be character-for-character what the page says. Titles are as the search returned them; a few came back as lower-case URL slugs (REI newsroom, TODAY, halfwayanywhere, trailandkale) or as a site banner (Highsnobiety 'Double Tap to Zoom', Ulta 'www.ulta.com') and are given that way. (4) 'own page' means the store's own page or newsroom was in the search results with that text; I did not read it directly. Own-site URLs listed as a source without quoted terms (Old Navy, adidas, Ulta, J.Crew Factory) are the store's Black Friday page for reference only and did not supply the offer. (5) Year checks: DealNews post numbers were used as a rough date check (this November's posts are numbered about 22.37 to 22.42 million; two YETI/Dick's posts numbered 21.78 million were dropped as 2025). 2026 day-of-week fits were checked for the Ulta, REI, Bass Pro and Kohl's dates. (6) Several recorded waves are already over on November 22 (adidas First Access, Ulta Early Black Friday, Bath & Body Works 40% off, possibly Nike EARLYBF and DSW early sale); they are kept because the task asked for waves to be recorded separately, and each says so in 'terms'. (7) Four findings are brand sales at another retailer (Nike, Skechers and Levi's at Amazon; Sephora at Kohl's) and are labelled that way in 'store'. (8) The visualping.io and pagecrawl.io guides are third-party monitoring-site blog posts that report what the store pages showed on a given date; they are counted as an independent dated source, not as the store's own page. (9) The search tool often reported a statement without naming which result carried it. Where that happened I attached it to the most likely result and say so; in particular, for American Eagle and Nike the "as of November 17" statements came from one of the two monitoring-site guides listed (dates left null), the Old Navy "updated November 12" guide is taken to be the Visualping one, the Banana Republic Factory deal-site line is attached to a DealNews category page, the Academy and Sephora-at-Kohl's giveaways to the Hip2Save freebies post, and the lululemon "Specials went live" line to one of the two 9to5Toys roundups of November 21.

F2 - single products (kind \"product\").notes: Method limits the reader should know. (1) All 32 searches of the allowance were used (23 standard, 9 extended) and no page could be opened: the one page tried, www.thebump.com, is outside this session's allowed network, so could_open_pages is false. (2) Every quote is the wording the web-search result gave. Where the result reproduced a page's own line it is given as is; where it paraphrased, the quote starts with 'search result'. Titles are as the search results listed them. (3) The search tool returns a written summary plus a list of links, and often does not say which link a line came from. Where that happened the candidate pages are listed as sources and 'terms' says the page was not pinned. deal_site_posts is filled from those same sources, so a post listed there may be a candidate rather than the confirmed carrier; 'terms' says so each time. (4) 'Two sources' means two different sites gave the same price (or the same dollars-off). Two pages of one site count as one. 'Own page' means the search result showed the store's own page stating the offer; nothing was opened. (5) Many one-source findings come from shopping roundups (The Bump, SheKnows, Good Morning America, Yahoo, CNN) that did not name the retailer in the part the search showed; the store field says so rather than guessing. (6) Several entries have no dollar price (percent-off or dollars-off only: Petco Wisdom Panel, Ulta OLAPLEX, Ulta Dyson Airwrap, Shark code SPARKLE, BowFlex T6). They are kept because the task named those products, and their price is null rather than worked out. (7) Dates are filled only where a result stated them. 'where' is 'online' when the deal was seen as an online listing; in-store availability was not checked, except Ulta and Petco, which the results describe as in stores and online. (8) Texas: every store here ships nationwide or has Texas stores (Amazon, Walmart, Macy's, DSW, Zappos, Ulta, Petco, Chewy, Crocs, adidas, HOKA, YETI, Whisker, BowFlex, Shark); none of the offers was stated as region-limited. (9) Toys and auto got three searches and returned mostly expired early-sale listings; baby and pets came back thin on deal sites even with five searches each, so most baby prices come from parenting sites, not deal-site posts.
